title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: Payment of Documentation Fees
content:
Fees raised on documents of the `Bills of Lading and Transport Documents` range are settled by remittance against the individual document. This page sets out how a remittance is applied, how much of it can be booked and how documentation fees relate to the booking's freight account.

## Clauses

1. **One document per remittance entry.** A remittance is applied to the fees of a single document. It is recorded with the remittance reference exactly as the customer quotes it, character for character, and with the amount remitted.
2. **Ceiling.** The amount booked can never be more than the documentation charges due on that document. The booked amount is therefore the lower of the amount remitted and the charges due; any surplus is sent back by finance and is not booked.
3. **Reference used once.** A given remittance reference is recorded no more than once on the same document.
4. **Separate accounts.** Documentation fees and the booking's freight are kept apart. Money remitted against the booking does not discharge any documentation fee, and money remitted against a document does not discharge freight.

## Worked examples (hypothetical figures)

| Documentation charges due | Amount remitted | Amount booked | Returned by finance |
|---|---|---|---|
| 165.00 | 200.00 | 165.00 | 35.00 |
| 165.00 | 100.00 | 100.00 | nothing |
| 165.00 | 165.00 | 165.00 | nothing |

## Basis Q&A

**The customer paid the booking's freight invoice and believes the issuance fee is covered by it. Is it?** No. A payment against the booking does not reduce the documentation charges due on the document.

**The same remittance reference is quoted twice for one document. Is it recorded twice?** No. A reference appears only once per document.

**The reference contains spaces and lower-case letters. May it be tidied up?** No. It is recorded exactly as quoted.
